title: Cutting It Out
logline: A chena farmer finally decides to dig out, root and all, a weed that has come back every season for years, choosing the harder work now over the easier work every year after.

object.note: Object 10 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: Having reached the far bank, the question turns to what is left behind for good: a farmer digging out, root and all, a weed that has returned every season.

thread_out.thread: The weed that will not return becomes a pull that no longer comes: a shopkeeper who gave up an old trade and talks about not being pulled at all.

requirements: A working chena farmer with a real recurring weed problem
A filming schedule that can follow at least one full clearing
Ideally, a return visit the following season

suggestions.name: A chena farming area
suggestions.why: Slash-and-burn cultivation is still practised in parts of the dry zone.
suggestions.verify: A specific willing farmer must be identified.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed.

lesson.in_simple_terms: Managing a problem and ending it are different things: cutting a weed back keeps it quiet for a season, but digging out the root means it does not come back. The texts use this same difference for the deepest kind of change.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: ප්‍රශ්නයක් පාලනය කිරීමත් එය අවසන් කිරීමත් දෙකකි; වල් පැළයක් කපා දැමුවොත් ටික කලකට නිහඬ වුවත්, මුලින්ම ගලවා දැමුවොත් එය නැවත නොඑයි.
lesson.the_teaching: The texts say that ordinary good actions, and even deep absorption, only push harmful tendencies aside or hold them down for a while, and cannot carry a person across. The path minds (magga citta) instead cut them off at the root (samuccheda-pahāna), and each path arises only once because nothing is left for it to do again. The Pradeepika's image is a young mango tree: felling it does not touch the fruit already eaten, but the fruit that would have grown never appears. The texts also stress balance on the way: too much energy makes the mind restless, and too little makes it sluggish.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The film begins with the familiar weed found again this season and the farmer's decision about it. It then stays with the harder labour: roots traced and pulled rather than cut, patient digging that neither gives up nor forces the tool. The cleared ground, and the next season if filming allows, let the viewer judge for themselves whether it returns.

key_terms.en: path mind: arises once per stage and cuts off defilements for good

lesson.caution: This is not a quick fix: the texts say only the path cuts a tendency off at the root, and no single decision or act of willpower is presented as deleting a habit for good.
lesson.builds_on: The ferry reached the same far bank many ways; this film asks what is left behind for good, drawing on the texts' line between holding something down and cutting it at the root.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
